Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

answer.feedback: Search for a refinement of the inhibited-growth models, especially one that improves glucose consumption predictions without degrading biomass fit. The closest candidates (C40 and C17) both under-predict x2 in E3 and E2 (C40 worst at E3 t=11 h and E2 t=5 h; C17 at E3 t=4 h and E2 t=1 h). The simpler candidates also strongly under-predict E3 x2 late in the run, especially at t=20 h. This suggests their substrate-consumption response is too weak in those conditions—consider refining high-substrate inhibition or the coupling between growth and glucose uptake. Also investigate the early E1 biomass over-prediction (t=1 h) in C40 and C17, which may indicate an initial-transient or biomass-related mismatch.
answer.reasoning: No candidate meets the acceptance rule: every candidate has chi2 above its 95% limit. C40 is closest (151.3 vs 147.7), and its parameters are individually precise, but it still fails the fit criterion and only 2 of 4 starts reached that fit. C17 also fails (158.5 vs 147.7); the other candidates have much larger lack of fit, and C29 additionally has strongly correlated parameters.
